newsitem.title: USA: U.S. investigates possible Russian laser incident.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investigates possible Russian laser incident.

text.p: The Pentagon said on Wednesday a Russian merchant ship in U.S. waters may have illuminated a Canadian military helicopter with a laser last month, causing painful burns to two people on board.

But Army Col. Dick Bridges, a Pentagon spokesman, told reporters the merchant ship Kapitan Man was searched by the U.S. Coast Guard at Tacoma, Washington, three days after the April 4 incident and no laser device was found.
The Canadian pilot and a U.S. Navy lieutenant reported suffering painful burns to their eyes the day after the incident.

Bridges responded to questions on a report in Wednesday's Washington Times newspaper, which said the ship was suspected of spying on U.S. submarines, and the CH-124 Canadian Maritime Pacific Command helicopter was taking photographs of the ship.
"A Canadian military helicopter on the 4th of April was illuminated, or was suspected of being illuminated, by a suspected laser device aboard the Russian merchant ship Kapitan Man," Bridges said.
The incident occurred at midday five miles (eight km) northwest of Port Angeles, Washington, in U.S. territorial waters as the helicopter was taking pictures of the ship, he said.
Four Canadians and the U.S. Navy observer were aboard the helicopter, which was on routine patrol.
The Times reported the Kapitan Man may have been spying on the strategic missile submarine USS Ohio, which was in the area at the time.
Bridges told reporters that burns to the eyes of the two men caused pain on the day after the incident, but there was apparently no permanent damage to their eyes.

"The examining physician diagnosed their condition as consistent with damage caused by laser burns. However, it was not conclusive, it was consistent with what one might expect from a laser burn," Bridges said. "The doctor also did not feel that the damage would be permanent."
The Russian ship denied it had any laser device on board, the spokesman said, but he added that one of the photographs of the ship showed "a bright red spot coming from the bridge."
He said the photograph did not show what might have caused the spot.
Bridges said the Coast Guard notified the captain of the ship on April 7 that it would search the vessel, and a search of about two hours was conducted that night.
"The Coast Guard examined all spaces on the ship and found no laser device. The (ship) captain firmly denied that any such device was on the ship," he said.

The United States and other countries have conducted extensive experiments in the use of laser weapons that could disable or shoot down aircraft and even satellites, but the U.S. military has rejected the use of lasers designed to blind enemy soldiers.
Some ships carry small portable lasers as navigational aids, but there was no indication that the Kapitan Man had carried such a device, U.S. defence officials said.
